geometry_edits.rationale: Widen the ground-level bite so the access response reads as a more legible public seam rather than a small incision.
Increase the vertical extent of the notch to strengthen the public threshold and give the ground edge more spatial consequence.
Reduce the courtyard margin to carve a more usable and visible void while preserving the dominant compact mass.
Align the void opening with the verified access side so the public-space figure responds coherently to the frontage.

rationale: The candidate reads as one coherent compact mass in all four views, so it is not fragmented and the repair is geometrically stable. The west-side notch gives a basic public edge response, but the void is shallow and not especially legible as usable ground space. The overall silhouette is still mostly box-like with a small incision, so the dominant gesture is understandable but not strong. For neighborhood living, the form can plausibly support the brief, but it under-expresses active ground threshold and public-space logic, and the section does not yet communicate a more meaningful terrace/court relationship. The hard-gate fail is driven by the weak semantic response to the access edge and the insufficient void/publicness rather than any rendering issue.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Reference is pavilion-like and much more overtly public/commercial; candidate lacks the same canopy/threshold clarity.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Compact street-facing low-rise volume with a legible entry setback and attached vertical marker can support neighborhood commercial/public ground use.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Reference is a larger, more articulated midrise composition; candidate is simpler and less layered in section.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Mixed-use streetwall logic with attached volumes and a modest setback can preserve hierarchy while staying urban and compact.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Counterfactual reference is a different program and much more sectional/landform-driven than the candidate; use only the idea of void hierarchy, not the building type.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Terraced/courtyard massing can generate strong public-open-space relationships and stepped hierarchy.

warnings: Candidate appears to rely on a generic rectangular datum with a single notch; this is close to acceptable but not yet a compelling public-ground mass.
The access edge response is present but thin; it should become a clearer court, undercut, or entry seam aligned to the verified frontage.
Rejecting because the form is only mildly resolved in section/void logic, not because of aesthetics.
Solid consistency across views is acceptable; no obvious collision was detected.
